newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Head of Russian church prays for Yeltsin health.
newsitem.headline: Head of Russian church prays for Yeltsin health.

text.p: The head of the Russian Orthodox Church, Patriarch Alexiy II, called on Monday for prayers for ailing President Boris Yeltsin during his forthcoming heart surgery.

At a service of thanksgiving for an icon reputed to have saved Russia from western invaders in the 17th century, he called on the Virgin Mary and the faithful across the country to pray for the former communist's return to health.

"Heal the illnesses, the spiritual and corporeal ailments of the president of our Russian land, forgive him his transgressions, witting and unwitting, deliver him soon from his sickbed and restore him to good health," Alexiy said, leading prayers at the Kazan Cathedral facing the Kremlin on Red Square.

"It is our wish that the forthcoming operation on the president be successful, that the Mother of God beseech the Lord to bestow upon him health and strength so that he may further serve Russia and its people," the patriarch said, noting that Yeltsin was re-elected in a free election last July.

The church has thriven since Yeltsin, once a member of the Soviet politburo, helped lead Russia out of atheistic communism in 1991. The Kazan Cathedral, built to house the Our Lady of Kazan icon, was rebuilt two years ago after being demolished in the 1930s.

The icon was credited with bringing the Russians victory in 1612 over Polish invaders who had taken advantage of more than a decade of civil war and chaos provoked by the death of tsar Ivan the Terrible.
Russians frequently draw comparisons between their country's present upheavals and the early 17th century "Time of Troubles".
